blocks.content: The Competition Commission of India possesses broad regulatory, investigative, and quasi-judicial powers to eliminate practices having an appreciable adverse effect on competition in India.

rows: Collusive conduct between two or more market players/enterprises
Unilateral conduct by a single dominant enterprise or group
Agreement causing Appreciable Adverse Effect on Competition (AAEC)
Proof that the enterprise holds a dominant position in the relevant market
Horizontal (cartels, bid rigging) and Vertical agreements (resale price maintenance)
Predatory pricing, discriminatory conditions, leveraging, denial of market access
Up to 3x profit or 10% turnover for cartels (whichever is higher)
Up to 10% of average turnover for the preceding 3 financial years

items: For cartel violations under Section 3, CCI can impose a penalty of up to 3 times the profit for each year of agreement OR 10% of turnover, whichever is higher.
An appeal against any direction, decision, or order passed by the CCI lies with the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).
CCI has the power under Section 28 to order the division of an enterprise enjoying a dominant position to ensure it does not abuse its dominance.
CCI can issue interim orders under Section 33 restraining any party from carrying out an anti-competitive act during an ongoing inquiry.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways on Powers of CCI
items: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) is a statutory quasi-judicial body empowered to prohibit anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position, and regulate combinations.
Under Section 3, CCI inquires into anti-competitive agreements including horizontal cartels and vertical restraints that cause an Appreciable Adverse Effect on Competition (AAEC).
Under Section 4, CCI targets unilateral conduct by dominant enterprises engaging in unfair, discriminatory, or predatory pricing and denial of market access.
Under Sections 5 and 6, CCI regulates combinations (mergers, acquisitions, and amalgamations) above prescribed economic thresholds.
The Director General (DG) functions as the investigative wing of CCI, initiating detailed investigations upon a prima facie order issued under Section 26(1).
